hints: Read each statement very carefully and look for one structure in the wrong place, like a bacterial wall molecule in a plant or an animal organelle in every plant cell.
Recall your three quick checks: viruses have protein plus either DNA or RNA, peptidoglycan means bacteria, and prokaryotes have smaller 70S ribosomes while eukaryotes have larger 80S ribosomes.
walkthrough:
**Start With What Each Group Is**

Think side by side. Viruses are tiny and non-cellular, just nucleic acid in protein. Plants are eukaryotes with cellulose walls. Bacteria are prokaryotes with peptidoglycan walls and small ribosomes.

This big picture helps you spot what does not belong.

**Check Each Statement For Its Tricky Word**

Option B puts peptidoglycan in plants, but that is a bacterial wall molecule. Option C says all plant cells have centrioles, but most higher plant cells lack them. Option D gives prokaryotes 80S ribosomes, but they have 70S.

One wrong word makes the whole statement incorrect.

**Confirm The True Statement**

A virus is indeed a protein coat, called a capsid, surrounding either RNA or DNA, never both in the same virus. Some also have an envelope, but the core description is always correct.

So A is the only fully correct statement.

options.A: Correct, all viruses have nucleic acid (either RNA or DNA) surrounded by a protein capsid. Well done for remembering this core definition.
options.B: False, plant cell walls contain cellulose, while peptidoglycan (murein) is found only in bacterial prokaryotic cell walls.
options.C: False, plasmodesmata are found in plant cells but centrioles are generally absent from higher plant cells.
options.D: False, prokaryotic cells use smaller 70S ribosomes for protein synthesis, while 80S ribosomes are found in eukaryotes.
